normal: A uniform grain structure. Grain colors cover the whole spectrum (purples, yellows, greens, blues, reds and pastel shades) in roughly equal amounts, mixed at random. No color family dominates, and grains of similar color do not cluster into a region or band.
defective: A non-uniform grain structure. One color family dominates (for example many red grains), or two color families dominate (for example many cyan or turquoise grains together with many red, orange or brown grains, and few purple, yellow or pastel grains), or grains of similar color form a band or region.
